title: Capability gates and telemetry handoff for RBAC v2 migration
content:
Purpose:
This note documents a pragmatic gate-based rollout strategy that couples capability-level feature flags ("capability gates") with a lightweight telemetry handoff shim for evidence enrichment and SIEM export. The goal is to enable incremental RBAC v2 behavior (fine-grained entitlements + attestation metadata) without blocking product teams, and to provide clear telemetry/forensics for every migration step.

Scope and constraints:
- Covers core authorization checks (invoke, read, admin) and entitlements surface for hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control plane.
- Focus is on observable handoff for SIEM and evidence automation (not full policy language).
- Must not change user-facing resource names; we introduce capability ids and tags that map to existing resource URNs.
- Low-touch oncall expectations during canaries; reversible feature flags.

High-level approach (TL;DR):
1) Introduce capability gates as runtime flags per-tenant. Each gate represents a guarded capability (e.g., "model.invoke", "console.create-route").
2) Implement an evidence-handoff shim in the authorization library that attaches a minimal evidence envelope to every decision. The envelope is the unit exported to SIEM or downstream evidence automation.
3) Canary: route 1% of tenants (by org-id hash) to RBAC-v2 enforcement mode where gates are enforced; all others stay in permissive mode with logging of the same envelope (no enforcement).
4) Iterate telemetry schema and enrichment fields before broader rollout.

Capability gate model (runtime):
- gate_id: short identifier (capability:model.invoke).
- gate_state: off | permissive | enforce | shadow-enforce.
  - permissive: allow, emit envelope indicating what would have happened if enforced.
  - shadow-enforce: evaluate and emit decision and evidence, keep previous enforcement decision (for safety).
  - enforce: apply RBAC v2 decision.
- per-tenant override: list of gate exceptions (temporary allow/deny) with expiry.

Evidence handoff shim (library-level behavior):
- Execute authorization check -> decision + rule_trace + attributes.
- Construct evidence envelope and attach to request context and any audit event.
- Push envelope to local telemetry buffer and to async exporter for SIEM (batch + compress).
- Envelope must be small (goal < 2KB) and stable across SDK versions.

Minimal evidence envelope schema (example exported to SIEM):
{
  "ts": "2025-02-12T18:04:22Z",
  "event_type": "authorization.check",
  "user": "user:alice@redwood.com",
  "action": "invoke-model",
  "resource": "model:llama-2-70b:deployed:prod",
  "result": "denied",
  "policy_id": "capability:model-invoke:v2",
  "evidence_ids": ["entitlement:team-x","attestation:session-389"],
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "metadata": {"seq_len":"512","quant_profile":"q4_0"},
  "agent_version": "rbaclib-2.1.0",
  "sig_v": "v1"
}

Notes on the envelope above:
- Keep keys predictable and snake-case.
- "metadata" is a free-form map for small context; avoid PII.
- "evidence_ids" are lightweight handles; the full evidence snapshot should live in an evidence datastore and be retrievable by id (not inlined in SIEM).

SIEM export considerations:
- Exporter batches envelopes per org and sends to SIEM with authentication and retry semantics.
- Use a two-tier export: immediate critical-enforcement events (deny under enforce mode) and async bulk for permissive/shadow events.
- Add a delivery-status telemetry metric (sent/failed/backoff) per org.

Rollout gates and success criteria:
Phases:
- Phase 0: library + schema landed in CI; unit tests and contract tests between auth library and exporter.
- Phase 1 (Shadow logs): 1% tenants -> permissive with envelope emission; validate schema, SIEM parsers, and enrichment jobs. Metrics: <1% parsing errors, 99.9% delivery for critical events within 2m.
- Phase 2 (Shadow-eval): 5% tenants -> shadow-enforce mode. Track mismatches against legacy enforcement for false denies/permits. Acceptance: false-positive rate <0.5% for model-invoke in 2 weeks.
- Phase 3 (Canary enforce): 1% tenants -> enforce mode with rollback window 24hrs. Oncall escalation if >0.1% increase in 5xx or >0.5% customer escalations.
- Phase 4 (Ramp): gradual ramp to 50% then 100% over multi-week with iterative fixes and evidence enrichment.

Canary measurement dashboard (minimum):
- per-tenant auth decision counts by gate and mode (enforce/shadow/permissive).
- decision mismatches (legacy vs v2) and top 10 resource types with mismatches.
- SIEM export delivery lag histogram.
- Evidence store retrieval success rates.

Migration runbook (short checklist):
- Preflight: static analysis of tenant entitlement shapes (Jira: SEC-923).
- Data freeze window for entitlements mapping (small read-only snapshot).
- Run reconciliation job to map old entitlements to capability ids (script located in github link).
- Launch Phase 1 gate for targeted tenant cohort.
- Validate SIEM parser and TTR (time-to-resolve) on sample deny cases.
- If mismatch spike: flip tenants to permissive for 1 hour, create postmortem.

Outstanding risks and mitigation notes:
- Risk: evidence envelope leaks PII. Mitigation: strict allowlist for metadata keys; runtime scrubber.
- Risk: SIEM ingestion cost explosion due to shadow logs. Mitigation: sampling (default 10% for permissive mode), org-level knobs.
- Risk: operational burden on CS for denied calls. Mitigation: temporary auto-allow tokens for impacted routes and an automatic rollback playbook.

Implementation notes for engineers (practical):
- Add a compact proto for the envelope (proto evolves; exporter accepts v1/v2 with compatibility).
- Keep the runtime decision fast: authorization lib should cache tenant capability maps with TTL 30s and watch for config updates.
- Evidence store: append-only, indexed by evidence_id, retention 365d by default. Provide pre-compiled lookup lambda for SIEM enrichers.
- Exporter: support backpressure and disk buffering for Private deployments.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Do we need cryptographic signing for evidence_id bundles? (tradeoff: cost vs tamper detection)
- Mapping rules for composite resources (e.g., multi-model compositions) need policy examples.
- How to surface manual review requests from evidence store to CS queue in a privacy-preserving way?

Quick links and references:
- Confluence: RBAC v2 overview (linked above)
- Migration script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/678
- Relevant Jira tickets: JIRA-SEC-8423, JIRA-SEC-923, JIRA-OPS-1109

Appendix: short sample migration shim pseudocode:
- check = authlib.check(user, action, resource, context)
- envelope = authlib.build_envelope(check, context)
- telemetry.emit(envelope)
- if gate_state == "enforce": return check.decision else return legacy_decision

End of doc.

Notes: this is intentionally operational and focused on telemetry/forensics handoff rather than full policy syntax; followup doc will contain mapping tables and example rule translations per product route.
